conventions.convention: RMSProp has no momentum or bias correction and adds a strictly positive ε outside the second-moment square root. A finite horizon may be zero.
Adam is scalar, uncorrected, initialized with zero moments, uses α/√t and denominator √(v_t+ε), and clips each update to [-1,1]. Inputs require v_t+ε>0.

AMSGrad takes the coordinatewise historical maximum of raw second moments, applies no bias correction or stabilizer, leaves zero-weight tentative coordinates unchanged, and permits any minimizer of its weighted quadratic over a nonempty compact convex feasible set.
Vector coordinates are one-based abbreviations z_i=z(i-1), translating the published Euclidean supplier's zero-based function coordinates.
The zero-ε Adam counterexample covers every α>0 and fixed β₁<√β₂; the positive-ε counterexample fixes α=1/10, β₁=0 and β₂=1/45. Comparators are selected separately at each finite horizon.
The AMSGrad regret inequality allows arbitrary 0≤β₁,t≤β₁=β₁,₁ with β₁/√β₂<1; its square-root upper-regret consequence requires either β₁,t=β₁λ^(t-1), 0≤λ<1, or β₁,t=β₁/t.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite admissible run of the RMSProp, uncorrected Adam, or uncorrected AMSGrad procedures defined on this page, all moment coordinates are finite and all second-moment coordinates are nonnegative. Every denominator specified by the procedure is positive. For AMSGrad, a zero historical-maximum coordinate has zero current and previous first moments, and the raw second moment is positive whenever its historical maximum is positive; the zero-ratio convention is therefore consistent. Each weighted minimization over the compact feasible set attains a minimum.

At an AMSGrad round with a nonempty compact convex F, convex loss ℓ_t, g_t∈∂ℓ_t(x_t), α_t>0 and 0≤β₁,t<1, let q_t,i=√v̂_t,i and E_t(z)=Σ_{i:q_t,i>0}z_i²/q_t,i. For every u∈F, ℓ_t(x_t)-ℓ_t(u) is at most (‖x_t-u‖²_Qt-‖x_{t+1}-u‖²_Qt)/(2α_t(1-β₁,t)) + α_t E_t(m_t)/(2(1-β₁,t)) + β₁,t α_t E_t(m_{t-1})/(2(1-β₁,t)) + β₁,t ‖x_t-u‖²_Qt/(2α_t(1-β₁,t)).

For finite-horizon uncorrected AMSGrad with α_t=α/√t, α>0, β₂∈(0,1), 0≤β₁,t≤β₁<√β₂ and γ=β₁/√β₂, interpreting zero-denominator contributions as zero, Σ_t α_t Σ_i m_t,i²/√v̂_t,i ≤ α Σ_i Σ_t |g_t,i|/√t divided by ((1-β₁)(1-γ)√(1-β₂)).
Let n≥1, x₀∈[-1,1], k∈{0,…,n}, δ_j≤0 for j≤k and δ_j≥0 for j>k. Define c(y)=max{-1,min{1,y}} and x_j=c(x_{j-1}+δ_j). Then x_n≥min{1,x₀+Σ_{j=1}^n δ_j}.
For every real q∈[0,1), every p∈{1,2}, and every real δ>0, there is an integer N≥1 such that n^p q^n<δ for every integer n≥N.

For every α>0 and fixed β₁<√β₂ in the stated Adam parameter ranges, some even C≥2 gives the ε=0 periodic slopes C,-1,…,-1, initialized at x₁=1, with liminf R_T/T≥2/C. For every fixed ε>0, α=1/10, β₁=0, β₂=1/45 and periodic slopes 3√ε,-√ε,-√ε give liminf R_T/T≥2√ε/3. Both claims use uncorrected scalar Adam with inside-root ε and clipping to [-1,1].

Under its nonempty compact convex domain, continuous convex losses, chosen bounded subgradients, finite coordinate-diameter bound, α_t=α/√t, β₁=β₁,₁, 0≤β₁,t≤β₁ and γ=β₁/√β₂<1 hypotheses, R_T(u)≤D∞²√T Σ_i√v̂_T,i/(2α(1-β₁)) + D∞² Σ_{t,i}β₁,t√v̂_t,i/α_t divided by (1-β₁)² + α Σ_{i,t}|g_t,i|/√t divided by ((1-β₁)²(1-γ)√(1-β₂)). The geometric and reciprocal first-moment schedules stated there give best-comparator regret O(√T).

No SGD stationarity conclusion is restated as an adaptive-method result.
